## Introduction

We ask how strongly health and well-being are associated across the
studies included in the selected `HealthWellbeing` dataset version.
The input consists of study summaries from the teaching example in
*Doing Meta-Analysis with R: A Hands-On Guide*.
[Section 4.2.4, Correlations](https://doing-meta.guide/pooling-es#correlations)

```{r health-report-input, include = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
# The summary path is relative to the project root, wherever Quarto runs.
summary_file <- here::here(params$summary_file)
result <- utils::read.csv(summary_file, colClasses = "character")
stopifnot(nrow(result) == 1L, result$effect_scale == "ZCOR")
stopifnot(
  all(c("tau_method", "interval_method") %in% names(result)),
  !anyNA(c(result$tau_method, result$interval_method)),
  all(nzchar(c(result$tau_method, result$interval_method)))
)
numeric_fields <- c("pooled_r", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "confidence_level")
result[numeric_fields] <- lapply(result[numeric_fields], as.numeric)

tau_method <- switch(
  result$tau_method,
  REML = "restricted maximum likelihood (REML)",
  PM = "the Paule–Mandel method (PM)",
  DL = "the DerSimonian–Laird method (DL)",
  result$tau_method
)
interval_method <- switch(
  result$interval_method,
  HK = "the Hartung–Knapp method (HK)",
  KR = "the Kenward–Roger method (KR)",
  classic = "a normal approximation (classic)",
  result$interval_method
)

pipeline_md5 <- result[["pipeline_md5"]]
if (is.null(pipeline_md5)) {
  pipeline_md5 <- "unrecorded"
}
```

## Methods

The analysis pools Pearson correlations on Fisher's z scale with a
random-effects model. The pipeline estimates between-study variance
using `r tau_method` and calculates a confidence interval using
`r interval_method`. It transforms the estimate and interval limits
back to the correlation scale. Similarity of effect definitions and
independence of study estimates are assumptions of this analysis.

## Results

The analysis combined `r result$studies` studies. The pooled
correlation was `r sprintf("%.3f", result$pooled_r)` with a
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * result$confidence_level)` confidence interval
from `r sprintf("%.3f", result$ci_lower)` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", result$ci_upper)`.

The pooled estimate summarises the association across the included
studies. The studies differ in their populations and measurements,
so the association may vary between settings, and these observational
estimates do not show that better health causes greater well-being.
